desirous

dih-ZY-ruhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Desirous is having or expressing a strong wish for something.

Desirous of privacy after the scandal, the family stopped answering their phone entirely.

Example

Desirous of a life away from cameras, the retired actress bought a farmhouse under a different name.

The sentence names exactly what she wanted -- a private life -- and desirous simply signals that strong wish.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

wishful: Wishful is hope drifting ahead of reality -- wishful thinking half-believes something simply because it would be lovely. Desirous is stronger and more grounded: a real, strong wish for something, plainly felt and often acted on. The wishful daydream floats; the desirous person concretely wants.

eager: Eager is keyed-up readiness for something that is coming -- a race about to start, a trip already booked. Desirous looks further out: a strong wish to have or reach something you do not yet possess, whether or not anything is scheduled. Eagerness waits at the door; being desirous needs no date at all.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

indifferent: having no particular interest

satisfied: content with what one already has

Where it sits · how deep the craving runs — interested → desirous → yearning

interested vs. desirous: Interested is weaker than desirous: an interested person merely gives something curiosity and attention, while someone desirous feels a much stronger, active wish to have it.

yearning vs. desirous: Yearning is more intense than desirous: to be desirous is to strongly wish for something, but yearning goes deeper, an aching, often wistful longing that will not let go.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — desire

root — desire: a strong wish or longing for something (Latin desiderare)

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Desirous is simply desire ('a strong wish for something') plus -ous, 'full of.' Someone desirous of something is, quite literally, full of desire for it.

Use the root in a new word: desire

Use the root in a new word: desire: His only desire after the long expedition was a hot shower and a full night's sleep.

Word Choice

Desirous is fairly formal -- in conversation, most people would just say 'eager for' or 'hoping for' instead.
